chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him: When does ghusl (ritual bath) become obligatory upon the man and the woman? He said: When he inserts it, then ghusl, the mahr, and rajm become obligatory.

key_terms.أَدْخَلَهُ: he inserted it; the act of penetration that triggers the ruling
key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man upon whom the ruling applies
key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: the legal punishment of stoning in the relevant juridical context
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath that becomes obligatory after sexual intercourse
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman upon whom the ruling applies
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: the dower that becomes established through consummation

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory for a man and a woman according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that ghusl (ritual bath) becomes obligatory for both the man and the woman upon penetration. It also links that act to other legal consequences, including the establishment of mahr and rajm in their respective legal contexts.
